findings.text: Address translation emulation for stage one at EL1 and EL0, for stage one at EL2, and for combined stage handling is available to other components in this dossier through dedicated helpers that accept a virtual CPU, an operation selector and a virtual address.

Generic stage one translation that fills caller supplied walk state, plus a helper that locates the page table level backing a virtual address and intermediate address pair, are available to other components in this dossier.

The EL1 EL0 helper attempts a hardware translation first and on certain failures falls back to a software walk, finally storing the resulting value in PAR_EL1 and reporting either success or a restart request.

The EL2 helper adjusts virtualization controls around a hardware translation, restores them, and on failure without a permission indication replays the operation in software before storing to PAR_EL1.

The combined stage helper rewrites its selector to a stage one form, performs stage one emulation, then when two stages are active derives an intermediate address and walks the nested second stage, checks direction dependent readability or writability, and folds the outcome into PAR_EL1.

The generic translate helper prepares walk state, grants full permissions when the first stage is disabled, otherwise walks and computes permissions. The level finder prepares filtered walk state, walks under protection, and maps interruption versus completion versus error to level output versus not found versus failure.

Indirect handling derives an index from the descriptor, then for the EL10 regime reads privileged permissions from PIR_EL1 and unprivileged from PIRE0_EL1, for the EL20 regime from PIR_EL2 and PIRE0_EL2, and for the EL2 regime from PIR_EL2 while forcing unprivileged to denied. Override flags reflect whether the high permission bit is clear combined with separate overlay enable inputs.

Each four bit permission value determines a read write execute triple for one privilege view, with several values denying everything, write never granted without read, execute granted only by a subset, a separate never write executable flag set for exactly one value, and a configuration where privileged execute coincides with unprivileged write collapses both views to denied.

Overlay handling extracts an index from the descriptor mask, then for privileged override selects among POR_EL1 and POR_EL2 by regime, and for unprivileged override selects POR_EL0 for EL10 and EL20 while forcing denied for EL2. Values using bits outside the three allowance bits collapse to none. Overlay write is cleared when the matching never write executable flag and overlay execute coincide, and base permissions are intersected with overlay allowances only when the corresponding override flag holds.

Stage one permission computation chooses direct or indirect base handling from a feature enable, applies hierarchical restrictions unless disabled, then applies overlay handling, then applies fallback never write executable suppression when overlay is inactive, and finally suppresses privileged access under privileged access never rules that consider unprivileged readability and writability and optionally executability.

Permission and access failures are recognized by masking the fault status field from PAR and comparing its type portion against permission or access encodings while requiring the stage two indicator to be clear.

Each register bit to feature entry carries either a bit pattern or a pointer to fine grained trap masks distinguished by a flag, plus a flags word, plus either an identifier register field locator with position width signedness and lower limit or a predicate over the virtual machine, with a set bit forcing unconditional reserved handling.

Capability macros each bind a symbolic feature name to one architecture identifier register field and a minimum level, allowing register descriptions to declare per bit feature requirements uniformly.

Fast hardware translation paths hold mmu_lock in write mode with interrupts saved across any temporary system register and stage two context switching and the hardware translation itself, restoring prior state before release.

Software page table walks in the slow address translation path and the combined stage second stage walk and the descriptor level search all execute under srcu read side protection for the virtual machine, with the slow path using explicit acquire and release around the walk and the others using scoped protection.
The map starts with a choice between bits and masks, then flags, then a choice between a locator holding regidx and shift and width and sign and lo_lim versus a match predicate.
The descriptor holds name and feat_map and bit_feat_map with bit_feat_map_sz.
The carrier holds ipa and level, used as private state threaded through filtered walks.

EL1 EL0 emulation starts with a fast hardware attempt. If the result signals failure without indicating a stage one permission or access fault, a software walk is run and may request restart. Otherwise the hardware result is kept. The final value is stored to the guest PAR.

EL2 emulation enters protected scope, adjusts virtualization controls including toggling nested bits when enhanced EL2 is clear, performs the mapped hardware operation, captures PAR on success, restores controls, and on failure without a permission indication replays in software before storing PAR.

Combined emulation maps its four selectors to stage one read or write forms with a direction flag, runs stage one emulation, exits early on stage one failure or when only one stage or neither virtualization nor default cache controls are active, otherwise builds an intermediate address from stage one output high bits plus original low bits, walks nested second stage, synthesizes a permission fault on direction mismatch, and merges into PAR.

Slow handling derives the translation regime from the operation, records whether the access is unprivileged and whether privileged access never applies, prepares walk state, short circuits when disabled, otherwise walks under protection, computes permissions, evaluates operation dependent readability or writability with address operations always passing, marks permission failure with a level dependent fault code, and builds PAR.

Level search selects EL20 versus EL2 versus EL10 regime from context, prepares filtered walk state with no unprivileged or never semantics, walks under protection invoking a filter that masks the sought address to walk granularity and compares against each table address, returning interruption on match, and maps interruption known as EINTR to level output and clean completion to not found and other codes to error.

A concurrent descriptor update during the slow walk is reported as EAGAIN that the caller propagates to restart the whole operation, and a missing second stage context for a nested virtual CPU causes the fast path to immediately return a failure PAR so the caller falls back to software.

Switching system register and stage two context behind the running guest requires interrupts disabled across the critical section. Unexpected operation selectors trigger a one time warning and forced failure in fast paths or an immediate fault in slow handling, and level search warns if the first stage is unexpectedly disabled.

NEVER_FGU corresponds to bit zero and CALL_FUNC to bit one and FORCE_RESx to bit two and MASKS_POINTER to bit three and AS_RES1 to bit four and REQUIRES_E2H1 to bit five and RES1_WHEN_E2H0 to bit six and RES1_WHEN_E2H1 to bit seven.

Permission index extraction uses four bit fields, and combined stage handling builds its intermediate address from stage one output covering bits forty seven through twelve combined with original address bits eleven through zero.
